transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Ross. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Ross. I am having a severe technical headache with our home broadband. Every twenty minutes, my corporate Cisco AnyConnect VPN drops its tunnel connection while I am working from home, throwing me out of my remote desktop session and corrupting my data files!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can help you troubleshoot local network MTU fragmentation, Heidi. First let's complete account verification. What is your full name and billing address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Heidi Lindqvist, 77 Westbourne Terrace, London, W2 3UY.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the four-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What router hardware model do you have installed on the connection?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We have the S-Net Hub 5 Pro connected to Openreach full fibre.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the general internet connection drop when the VPN disconnects, or is it strictly the Cisco AnyConnect tunnel?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: General browsing on websites like BBC works continuously, but the Cisco VPN tunnel drops dead every twenty minutes on the dot.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That symptom typically indicates IPv6 Path MTU blackholing where ICMPv6 'Packet Too Big' messages are being dropped by intermediate carrier nodes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My corporate IT department told me to call my ISP because your router is fragmenting packets! I cannot do my job as a financial analyst if my connection resets every twenty minutes! It is driving me crazy!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Consumer routers operate standard fifteen-hundred-byte frame sizes by default.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I know, but the VPN encapsulates headers and exceeds fifteen hundred bytes unless MSS clamping is configured.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously corporate VPN encapsulation requires appropriate MSS clamp adjustment to prevent buffer overflows.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do we adjust the MTU clamp on the Hub 5 Pro?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open your web browser and go to 192.168.1.1 to log into the router admin interface.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Logged into the Hub 5 Pro admin panel now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on 'Advanced Settings', then click on 'Broadband WAN Connectivity'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicked. It shows 'IPv4 MTU' and 'IPv6 MTU'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What are the numerical values currently configured in those two fields?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both are currently set to fifteen hundred bytes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Change both values from fifteen hundred down to fourteen twenty bytes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typed 1420 into IPv4 MTU, and 1420 into IPv6 MTU.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, does your corporate IT department enforce split-tunneling or full-tunneling over Cisco AnyConnect?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They enforce full-tunneling, so all web traffic routes through the office proxy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Full-tunneling adds an extra forty bytes of IPSec ESP overhead, which is why fourteen twenty was the exact sweet spot.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes total sense technically.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you don't have any secondary third-party mesh Wi-Fi pods attached to the Hub 5 Pro?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, just the standalone Hub 5 Pro in the hallway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That ensures there is no double-NAT encapsulation further down the chain.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know the network topology is completely clean.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now look below that for the checkbox labeled 'Enable MSS Clamping'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found it, it was unchecked. If this tunnel drops again during my audit presentation, my manager is going to escalate it!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Check the box for 'Enable MSS Clamping' and select 'Auto-Calculate from MTU'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checked and selected Auto-Calculate.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click 'Apply Changes'. The WAN interface will re-negotiate the PPPoE session. Bear with me for forty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Heidi. The WAN session has re-established with an MTU clamp of fourteen twenty bytes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does that do for the VPN tunnel?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the router specifications again. What router hardware model do you have installed on the connection?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you earlier, it's the Hub 5 Pro.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, the Hub 5 Pro hardware acceleration engine now automatically rewrites TCP SYN packet headers to constrain packet sizes to fourteen twenty bytes, preventing fragmentation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me launch Cisco AnyConnect and connect to our corporate gateway.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: AnyConnect is connected. Opening our Bloomberg terminal session...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the remote desktop terminal open without latency or dropped frames?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! The live market feed loaded immediately without the usual packet lag!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's run a continuous ping with fourteen hundred byte packets to verify zero fragmentation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running ping -l 1392 to our corporate server... Zero packet loss across fifty packets!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That proves packets are traversing the tunnel seamlessly without hitting MTU blackholes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That has completely fixed the drop-outs. I've been fighting with our corporate IT desk for two days over this!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will take direct ownership of this ticket and note the custom 1420 MTU setting on your account profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Ross, I really appreciate you taking ownership so future updates don't wipe it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your billing email address on file, it's heidi dot lindqvist at westbourne dot co dot uk, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my correct email.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm for the record, the installation address is 77 Westbourne Terrace, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 77 Westbourne Terrace.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your Hub 5 Pro or broadband line that I can assist you with today, Heidi?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Ross, that solved the exact technical problem. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Heidi, and have a great rest of your workday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Ross, goodbye.
